reason: Conversation 1 reached the correct hedged diagnosis (start relay/overload, with compressor failure as the alternative), asked sensible power and inspection questions, kept all work unplugged, and gave a usable relay swap procedure with an explicit fallback that repeated clicking means the compressor is seized and an engineer is needed; its weaknesses were a dropped turn, no condenser-cleaning advice, and no help identifying the exact part the customer asked for. Conversation 2 fired a boilerplate 'Stop using this appliance' warning that contradicted the customer's own report of no burning smell, never answered the resulting 'do I still need to stop using it' question, ignored the dusty condenser it had just asked about, and then refused to help further, escalating everything to an engineer. Escalation is acceptable, but the false safety alarm plus the unanswered question and the dead-end refusal left the homeowner more confused and less served than Conversation 1's honest, bounded guidance.
